recommendation.evidence_assessment: Moderate: preclinical rodent efficacy and community guidance strongly support defining candidate-level CMC/characterization requirements and controls, but key translational claims (intact-EV CNS exposure after intranasal dosing in large species; pre-specified potency/release criteria before cargo selection; manufacturability across scale) lack direct supporting data and require dedicated bridging experiments and process-validation data.
findings: Rodent intranasal EV studies show reproducible injury-model benefit but do not demonstrate quantitative intact-EV CNS exposure or guarantee cross-species translation.
MISEV2023 provides an orthogonal characterization framework that maps to necessary CMC and QC elements but does not define product-specific release limits or potency assays.

An immortalized/clonal MSC source is a plausible route to reduce source heterogeneity, but single-study activity data do not establish GMP-ready manufacturability, lot-to-lot potency consistency, or validated impurity clearance.

Non-human primate biodistribution data raise substantial risk that rodent intranasal exposure will not translate quantitatively to larger species, creating a gating requirement for a bridging biodistribution/PK/PD package.
objections: The proposed gate and minimum-definition plan assumes rodent intranasal intact-EV CNS delivery predicts larger species/human exposure and that a candidate-level potency/release specification can be fully defined prior to selecting therapeutic cargo — both assumptions are unsupported and make the candidate-definition premature and potentially uninformative for translation.

claim_updates.rationale: Multiple rodent studies show functional benefit; however, these data do not quantify intact-EV CNS exposure or cross-species translation.
claim_updates.statement: Rodent intranasal MSC-derived EVs show reproducible benefit in injury models and justify further candidate-defining and translational studies but do not by themselves demonstrate intact-EV CNS exposure in larger species.

claim_updates.rationale: Single-study activity from an immortalized line supports feasibility but lacks scale-up and GMP bridging data.
claim_updates.statement: An immortalized/clonal MSC source can reduce heterogeneity and is a plausible manufacturing route but is not sufficient without MCB/WCB, process validation, and lot-to-lot potency/stability data.

claim_updates.rationale: MISEV2023 defines orthogonal characterization and reporting expectations that translate into minimum CMC elements, but product-specific limits and validated assays remain to be generated.
claim_updates.statement: Minimum CMC must include a chosen source-cell with MCB/WCB plan, orthogonal EV identity/purity panel per MISEV, draft release specifications, stability-indicating assays, and a mechanism-linked potency assay to control biological activity across batches.

decision_update.question: Execute two-stage candidate-definition and biodistribution gate (source-cell/CMC definition then rodent+large-species biodistribution/PK/PD) before treating SGL-001 as candidate-like?
decision_update.rationale: Recommended to mitigate high translational risk from uncertain cross-species intranasal intact-EV delivery and to generate product-defining CMC and potency evidence needed for interpretable biodistribution and downstream efficacy studies.

proposed_changes.editorial_clarification: Potency assay specifics and numerical release limits cannot be finalized before selecting therapeutic cargo/mechanism; draft potency concepts are acceptable at this stage but must be validated against in vivo PD during the gate.

hypothesis_update.rationale: Bridging biodistribution and validated analytics are required to test cross-species translation and to tie in vitro potency concepts to in vivo PD.
hypothesis_update.statement: A two-stage gate (source-cell/CMC definition then rodent+large-animal biodistribution/PK/PD) will determine whether intranasal SGL-001 achieves reproducible intact‑EV CNS exposure and mechanism-relevant PD in a large species.
hypothesis_update.test_plan: Stage 1: finalize source-cell, create MCB/WCB, define orthogonal QC panel and draft release specs, run small-scale process dev and stability assays. Stage 2: biodistribution/PK/PD in rodents and a bridging large species (preferably NHP) with vehicle, free-label, and disrupted-EV controls; prespecified quantitative acceptance criteria for intact-EV CNS exposure, assay LLOQs/specificity, PK variability thresholds, and demonstration of mechanism-linked PD.

proposed_changes.next_action: Initiate the two-stage gate: (A) finalize source-cell, create MCB/WCB, define orthogonal QC panel and draft release specs, perform small-scale process dev; (B) run biodistribution/PK/PD bridging study in rodents and a large species (preferably NHP) with vehicle, free-label, and disrupted-EV controls and prespecified acceptance criteria.

risk_updates.description: Rodent intranasal biodistribution may not predict quantitative CNS exposure in larger species; NHP data suggest lower/variable CNS exposure and risk of dominant non-vesicular label signal.
risk_updates.mitigation: Require bridging biodistribution/PK/PD in a large species with validated intact-EV analytics and appropriate controls before advancement.
risk_updates.title: Cross-species uncertainty in intranasal intact-EV CNS delivery

risk_updates.description: Draft release specifications and potency concepts exist but lack validation, stability data, and lot-to-lot consistency across scaled runs.
risk_updates.mitigation: Establish MCB/WCB, orthogonal QC per MISEV, develop and validate potency assay linked to in vivo PD, and run multiple scale-up batches to demonstrate reproducibility.
risk_updates.title: CMC: identity, impurity control, and potency assay readiness

risk_updates.description: Efficacy evidence is from acute/injury rodent models; relevance to cognition/aging indications is unproven.
risk_updates.mitigation: Defer indication-specific efficacy studies until biodistribution/PD linkage is demonstrated; design follow-on efficacy models that reflect intended clinical endpoints.
risk_updates.title: Model generalizability from injury models to cognition/aging endpoints

recommendation.recommendation: Approve a mandatory two-stage candidate-definition and biodistribution gate before treating SGL-001 as a candidate-like product: (1) finalize source-cell choice and establish MCB/WCB; define orthogonal identity/purity QC panel and draft release specifications; develop a fit-for-purpose potency assay concept in parallel with small-scale process development; (2) execute a controlled biodistribution/PK/PD bridging package (rodent plus a large species, preferably NHP) that includes intact‑EV quantitative analytics with vehicle, free‑label, and disrupted‑EV controls, predefined acceptance criteria for CNS exposure and non-vesicular signal, and basic safety/tolerability. Require validated analytics that distinguish intact EV signal from label artifacts and demonstrate PK→PD linkage in the large species before advancement. Major therapeutic advancement decisions require human approval and should remain pending.
